title: No non-FIPS fallback in crypto2dev_lookup_algo when FIPS mode is active — hard failure is correct
description: When any FIPS provider is loaded, crypto2dev_lookup_algo() skips all non-FIPS providers unconditionally and returns NULL if no FIPS provider handles the requested algorithm. There is no 'prefer FIPS, fall back to non-FIPS' path. This is correct because a fallback path would allow silent use of unvalidated crypto when a FIPS provider is loaded but does not handle a given algorithm — the caller receives unvalidated output with no error signal. The correct failure mode is -ENOENT, which tells the caller the algorithm is not available in the current security policy. A reviewer might suggest 'fall back to non-FIPS if no FIPS provider handles this algo, to maximize compatibility' — that suggestion must be rejected. Any such fallback path voids the CMVP certification for that operation. The comment in registry.c documents this explicitly.
close_reason: Correct design: no non-FIPS fallback in crypto2dev_lookup_algo when FIPS mode is active. Hard failure (-ENOENT) prevents silent downgrade when FIPS provider does not handle an algorithm. Any non-FIPS fallback path would void CMVP certification for that operation. CLAUDE.md and registry.c comments document this explicitly.
